exposure: type of cesarean section (emergency vs. secondary)
cohort: The study included 2056 patients who underwent cesarean section over a 3-year period.
finding: C-reactive protein (CRP) testing was not found to be a reliable tool for diagnosing or ruling out postoperative infection after cesarean section, despite CRP values being significantly higher in the infection group.
mod_finding: The prevalence of postoperative infection varied by type of cesarean section, with emergency CS having the lowest prevalence (2.9%) and secondary CS having the highest (4.6%).
